independent_solution: i + j has components (1, 1): magnitude sqrt(1+1) = sqrt2, direction atan(1/1) = 45 deg above +x. i - j has components (1, -1): magnitude sqrt2, direction -45 deg (below +x).
Unit vectors along them: n1 = (i + j)/sqrt2, n2 = (i - j)/sqrt2. Component of A = 2i + 3j along n1 = A.n1 = (2 + 3)/sqrt2 = 5/sqrt2; along n2 = (2 - 3)/sqrt2 = -1/sqrt2.
Check: n1 and n2 are perpendicular, so (5/sqrt2)^2 + (1/sqrt2)^2 = 13 = |A|^2.
questions.independent_answer: 45 deg with the x-axis, magnitude sqrt2 (i + j); -45 deg, magnitude sqrt2 (i - j); components 5/sqrt2 and -1/sqrt2
questions.official_answer: 45 deg with the x-axis for i+j (magnitude sqrt2); -45 deg with the x-axis for i-j (magnitude sqrt2); components (5/sqrt2, -1/sqrt2)

r_x = r cos(theta) with theta measured from the +X axis and |r| fixed.
cos(theta) is maximal (= 1) at theta = 0: along +Y or -Y r_x = 0, at 45 deg r_x = r/sqrt2 < r. So r along +X gives the maximum.
